themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2,300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting either a sudden influx of unlicensed operators or enforcement gap in Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Community board has made repeated requests for more frequent litter basket collection, suggesting baseline sanitation concerns
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed food vendors clustering in specific neighborhoods (Fort Washington Ave corridor, parks)? Interview DOH about enforcement capacity.
Has a particular event, fair, or street fair permit triggered the spike? Cross-check with Parks Dept permits.

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints jumped to 18 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 1.9 per week—an 860% spike (z-score: 12.71)—indicating sudden traffic, congestion, or parking violations tied to ride-hailing services in the district.
evidence: 18 for-hire vehicle complaints last week vs. 1.9 weekly average (860% increase)
Z-score of 12.71 (severity: high) indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Illegal parking is already the 4th-highest complaint category (2,602 over 90 days), suggesting underlying street management issues
reporting_angles: Are Uber/Lyft drivers congregating near transit hubs (subway stations, commercial areas) causing gridlock or double-parking? Map complaint locations.
Has a TLC enforcement operation ended or relocated? Check with TLC on patrol coverage changes in CD 112.

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints spiked to 23 LAST WEEK from 4.4 per week average—a 426% increase (z-score: 9.98)—indicating acute deterioration, trip hazards, or emergency repair needs across Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 23 sidewalk condition complaints last week vs. 4.4 weekly baseline (426% spike)
Z-score of 9.98 indicates extreme deviation from historical pattern
Community board has repeated budget requests for street reconstruction/upgrades, suggesting chronic underinvestment in public realm
reporting_angles: Walk a major corridor (Broadway, Amsterdam Ave, Fort Washington Ave) and photograph sidewalk conditions. Identify patterns: water damage, tree root upheaval, pothole concentration.
Interview DOT and local council member on emergency repair backlog and capital plan timeline for CD 112 sidewalk work.

themes_detail.label: Water System Complaints Double
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints jumped to 42 LAST WEEK from 13.6 per week average—a 208% increase (z-score: 4.65)—coinciding with water conservation complaints up 220%, suggesting infrastructure strain, main breaks, or possible conservation emergency.
evidence: 42 water system complaints last week vs. 13.6 weekly baseline (208% spike)
6 water conservation complaints last week vs. 1.9 weekly average (220% increase)
Heat/hot water remains the top complaint category (7,654 over 90 days), indicating water-related services are a chronic district issue
reporting_angles: Has DEP issued water conservation notices or experienced a major main break in CD 112? Check DEP emergency logs and incident reports.
Interview residents about low water pressure, discolored water, or service disruptions. Map complaints to identify affected neighborhoods.

themes_detail.label: Industrial Waste & Environmental Concern
themes_detail.summary: Industrial waste complaints surged to 3 LAST WEEK from 0.2 per week average—a 1,100% spike (z-score: 4.16)—raising questions about illegal dumping, manufacturing activity, or hazardous material handling in residential Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 3 industrial waste complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1,100% spike)
Unsanitary conditions are 5th highest complaint category (1,343 over 90 days), indicating broader environmental stress in district
reporting_angles: Locate the 3 industrial waste complaints geographically. Are they clustered near a specific site, manufacturing plant, or waste facility?
Interview DSNY and DEP on enforcement actions and permits. Investigate whether new construction activity (364 DOB permits filed) is generating hazardous debris.
